name: Gamaliel
overview: The name Gamaliel appears in Scripture referring to two distinct individuals. One Gamaliel was a prominent leader of the tribe of Manasseh, serving as captain and prince during the wilderness period, as recorded in Numbers 1:10, 2:20, 7:54, and 10:23, where he is noted for his role in the organization and dedication of the tabernacle. Another Gamaliel, mentioned in the New Testament, was a celebrated teacher of the Jewish law who spoke wisely before the Sanhedrin and was the esteemed instructor of the Apostle Paul, who was trained at his feet in the perfect manner of the law (Acts 5:33; 22:3). Together, these references highlight Gamaliel’s significance both as a tribal leader in Israel’s early history and as a respected rabbinic figure influencing the early Christian witness.
